title: CI performance sheriff: multi-signal fusion for token/sec and p95 regression gating
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: Our current CI perf gating focuses on single-metric snapshots (tokens/sec p95) and produces two kinds of costly outcomes: noisy false positives triggered by sample variance or cold cache effects, and missed slow regressions that only appear under specific sequence-length mixes. Goal: Build a CI 'sheriff' that fuses multiple signals (tokens/sec, latency p95, cold vs warm cache indicators, variance, resource usage) and compares against a rolling, contextual baseline with robust statistical tests. The sheriff should run automatically on PRs that change serving code or runtime dependencies and produce deterministic artifacts (bench traces, per-shard p95 distribution, Bayesian posterior, summary) to be posted to the PR. If a validated regression is detected, the sheriff will block the PR and provide remediation guidance and a one-click rollback link for the canary deployment.
acceptance_criteria: CI job executes bench harness for changed components and collects tokens/sec and latency traces
Multi-signal detector produces a single pass/fail verdict and posts a detailed artifact link to the PR
False positive rate <= 2% on historical testbed (running simulation replay of last 90 days of commits)
Detects >=10% regression in tokens/sec p95 on baseline-simulated regressions in >=95% of injected test cases
Artifacts stored in perf-artifacts S3 with immutable run id and accessible dashboard link
Blocking behavior integrates with GitHub checks API and provides clear next steps in the PR comment
implementation_plan: Extend bench-runner CI image to emit detailed time-series traces and resource metrics per shard
Implement fusion layer as a lightweight service (perf-sheriff) that ingests traces and applies Bayesian change-point detection + robust effect-size thresholds
Create a contextual baseline store (rolling 7/14/30-day windows) keyed by model, sequence-length distribution, runtime config
Add adaptive thresholds that adjust based on sample size and observed variance to avoid cold-start false positives
Wire perf-sheriff to GH checks and to post an artifact ZIP with a summary JSON, HTML dashboard snapshot, and raw traces
Add integration test harness to simulate regressions and measure FPR/TPR in CI (keep as a separate nightly job)
testing_plan: Unit tests for fusion logic covering edge cases (tiny sample sizes, non-stationary traffic)
Historical-replay simulation: run sheriff across last 90 days of benchmark runs to verify FPR <= 2%
Synthetic-injection tests: automatically inject latency throttles and quantify detection recall for a range of regressions (5%..50%)
Canary blocking validation: run on internal repo PRs (non-production) for two sprints and compare human reviewer decisions vs sheriff verdict
Load test the perf-sheriff service itself to ensure <1s decision latency for typical PRs and graceful degradation if downstream baselines unavailable
updates: 2025-02-03 — Created initial ticket and high-level design. Noted overlap with ENG-35021 (continuous-throughput-sentinel) and ENG-37234 (stochastic-load-guardrail); will coordinate to avoid duplicate detectors.

2025-02-07 — Spike completed: bench-runner can now emit per-token time series and CPU/GPU CUDA metrics. Proof-of-concept fusion notebook shows improved precision when combining variance and cold-cache flags.

2025-02-11 — Design review with PM/Design: agreed to surface a single verdict and a human-readable summary plus links to three artifacts (summary HTML, raw traces, dashboard). PM asked for explicit remediation guidance in PR comment.

2025-02-14 — Implemented baseline store schema and rolling window logic. Chose 7/14/30 windows keyed by (model-version, seq-length-bucket, runtime-variant). Initial metrics show baseline drift during large data loads — added normalization by request distribution.
2025-02-18 — Prototype perf-sheriff deployed to staging CI. Ran a backtest on a 30-day window; recall on injected regressions was 96% and simulated FPR ~1.6%.
2025-02-20 — In-progress: wiring GH checks and artifact upload. Pending decision on whether to gate on all infra-affecting PRs or only runtime/library changes (requested input from infra team).
notes: Trade-offs considered: aggressive gating reduces regressions reaching prod but increases friction for engineering; we biased toward conservative adaptive thresholds and provide an override flow for urgent PRs.
We chose Bayesian change-point detection for better uncertainty quantification versus simple t-tests given small sample sizes on some PRs.
Long-term: plan to feed sheriff outputs into the console rollouts page so on-call can see historical regressions tied to model/runtime changes.
